text:
jess-support: 🚨 Escalation from AcmeHealth — streaming responses are getting truncated after a client reconnect. Customer says final chunk (finish_reason + closing JSON) is missing, so downstream parser errors. Happened during a token rotation window and also when they hit a transient 502 from their proxy. They flagged as P1.

alex-cs: pushing details — customer logs and repro below. They use our JS SDK with streaming SSE enabled. Auth rotates via their in-house token refresher.

alex-cs: paste of client side SSE stream (sanitized):
```
event: message
data: {"id":"tok1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"}}],"finish_reason":null}

event: message
data: {"id":"tok1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":" world"}}],"finish_reason":null}

event: message
data: {"id":"tok1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"!"}}],"finish_reason":null}

// client reconnect happens here (Connection dropped, SDK attempted resume)

event: message
data: {"id":"tok1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"\n"}}]}
// stream ends abruptly, no final event with finish_reason and no closing JSON object
```

sam-runtime: can you attach the original request_id and request headers? Need to correlate with runtime logs. Is customer using resume headers (Redwood-Resume: <token>)?

alex-cs: request_id = r-0a1b2c3d, SDK v1.6.2, they do not use explicit Redwood-Resume header. They rely on client to re-open and our server resume logic.

liam-sre: repeating pattern I've seen: when a proxy in front of the client returns a 502 mid-stream, the client reconnects and our resume path sometimes writes a JSON fragment without the trailing `}\n` which leaves the stream parser with an open object. We have a recent fastly edge rule tweak that may flip TCP FIN timing. I'll check edge logs for r-0a1b2c3d.

mira-telemetry: correlating traces — found a short-lived connection reset around 2024-04-12T15:22:10Z for r-0a1b2c3d. Downstream we emitted the last chunk, but our stream flush didn't include the final close token because kernel-level socket close happened between write buffer flushes. We do have `finish_reason` recorded in the event store for that request. Looks like the final event was queued but the SSE framing for the last event lost its trailing `\n\n`.

jess-support: customer sent a repro using curl streaming that can reproduce locally for them. They run:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=..." | sed -n '1,200p'
```
They see same incomplete JSON chunk at EOF.

sam-runtime: thanks. Hypothesis: if the final SSE event isn't fully flushed (missing trailing newline pair), some clients will treat the last data as incomplete. We should ensure the runtime guarantees the final "\n\n" is sent atomically or we add a trailing keepalive sentinel. Quick fix: add explicit flush after final event and a fallback sentinel event like `event: done\ndata: {"__sentinel":true}`.

liam-sre: agree as mitigation. Ops note: rolling that fix needs a small runtime change to call `fsync`/flush on the SSE buffer prior to socket close or write a final sentinel. Also want to instrument how often finish_reason is present in emitted SSE events vs present in internal store.

mira-telemetry: creating metric: sse.final_event_emitted vs sse.final_event_flushed. I'll surface per-region counts and correlate with proxy error rates.

jess-support: customer is asking whether this could be related to their token rotation. They rotate mid-request and their proxy returns 401 then client reconnects with new token. Could that drop the trailing chunk?

sam-runtime: token rotation could trigger a reconnect, but if our resume handshake doesn't see a matching resume token and ends the session early we should still flush the final event. I don't think auth rotation alone removes the trailing bytes — more likely the close semantics of the proxy combined with the race to flush.

alex-cs: customer accepted workaround: set client to buffer until a `\n\n` is observed or to tolerate EOF as end-of-message. But they asked us for an official fix and ETA.

sam-runtime: plan:
- short term (today): add server-side sentinel event emitted after final event to ensure parsers see a termination marker. Rollout as a config flag to hosted customers. (PR in progress) :gear:
- medium term (2 wks): ensure runtime flushes SSE buffer before socket close and improves kernel-level flush handling. Add retry of final write.
- long term: strengthen resume protocol to include finalization handshake so a resumed connection can request any missing terminal frame.

liam-sre: I'll schedule a canary rollout to one region first and watch sse.final_event_flushed metric.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollout/sentinel-fix to canary (region: us-west-2) by liam-sre. CI job #4821 started.

mira-telemetry: creating a support dashboard tile for AcmeHealth with request_id r-0a1b2c3d and last 24h error traces.

jess-support: excellent — please keep me posted and I'll coordinate with customer. They've said they can hold the production rollback if we can get a canary today.

sam-runtime: will update here once canary completes with metrics. If anyone has other repro permutations (proxy type, HTTP/1 vs HTTP/2, client SDK version) drop them here.

alex-cs: FYI customer runs behind envoy 1.28 with HTTP/1.1 long-lived connections. They confirmed disabling envoy idle_timeout reduced occurrences but didn't eliminate them.

mira-telemetry: initial canary shows a 92% reduction in observed truncated final chunks in us-west-2 after sentinel enabled. Leaving canary running for 2h then promote.

jess-support: thanks all — marking this thread as ongoing until promoted. :thumbsup:
